test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question: In ΔLMN, LM = 5sqrt 2 cm, LN = 13 cm and ∠LMN = 135°. What is the length (in cm) of MN?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Extend base MN to point P such that LP ⊥ PN. ΔLPM is a 45°−45°−90° triangle since ∠LMP = 45°.

LP = MP = LM ÷ √2 = 5√2 ÷ √2 = 5 cm.

In right ΔLPN, PN = √(LN² − LP²) = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm.

MN = PN − MP = 12 − 5 = 7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** LM = 5√2 cm, LN = 13 cm, ∠LMN = 135°

**Formula Used:** Cosine Rule → b² = a² + c² − 2ac cos(B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5757997624e09046ee19f7746c7bb7bf40891c52cad58d6bc9b1bde96f5aeb88.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let length MN = x cm.

⇒ LN² = LM² + MN² − 2 × LM × MN × cos(∠LMN)

⇒ 13² = (5√2)² + x² − 2 × (5√2) × x × cos(135°)

⇒ 169 = 50 + x² − 10√2x × (−1/√2)

⇒ 169 = 50 + x² + 10x

⇒ x² + 10x − 119 = 0

⇒ x² + 17x − 7x − 119 = 0

⇒ x(x + 17) − 7(x + 17) = 0

⇒ (x + 17)(x − 7) = 0

⇒ x = 7 or x = −17

⇒ Since side length cannot be negative, MN = 7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cosine Rule

It relates the sides and one angle of a triangle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos(C). It is useful when two sides and an included angle or all three sides are known.

Sine Rule

It relates sides to the sines of their opposite angles: a/sin(A) = b/sin(B) = c/sin(C). It is used to find unknown sides or angles when ratios are given.

Obtuse Triangle Properties

In an obtuse triangle, the square of the side opposite the obtuse angle is always greater than the sum of the squares of the other two sides (c² > a² + b²).</p
